findings.title: askHuman now runs automatically, which breaks the human-in-the-loop flow.
findings.body: Before this change, `askHuman` was a `tool()` with no `execute`. Generation stopped at the tool call and waited for the human's answer, which `humanResponseAsToolCall` later saves as the tool result. With `createTool` and a handler that returns `question`, the SDK runs the tool right away. It stores the question itself as the tool result and lets the model carry on, so the model never waits for the human. When a human does answer later, a second tool-result is saved for the same `toolCallId`. Fix: keep a tool with no executor, e.g. `tool({ description, inputSchema: z.object({...}) })` from "ai".

findings.title: `as any` casts added across the examples, against the PR's stated goal.
findings.body: The PR says it removes all `as any` assertions, but it adds them to `chat` in every agent, to the RAG embedding models (ragAsPrompt, ragAsTools), to `initialMessage` in threads.ts, and to the tool output in human.ts. In threads.ts, `initialMessage` comes from the client and is validated with `vMessage`, so casting it means any shape mismatch with v5's `saveMessage` (for example `mimeType` vs `mediaType`) is no longer caught at compile time. Fix: correct the types instead of casting.

findings.title: Adds the unchecked type assertion the PR says it removed.
findings.body: The PR description says `(input as { question: string }).question` was replaced with a runtime type check, but this line adds exactly that cast. If the model sends malformed input (`tc.input` undefined or missing `question`), it either throws or yields `undefined`, and nothing catches it. Fix: parse the input with the zod schema (`z.object({question: z.string()}).safeParse(tc.input)`) and skip or handle calls that fail.

findings.title: Chat model type goes back to LanguageModelV1, and the mismatch is hidden with `as any`.
findings.body: The PR is meant to add AI SDK v5 compatibility, but `chat` is now typed as `LanguageModelV1`, the v4 interface, while the providers return V2 models. The OpenAI branch hides the mismatch with `as any`. That forces every agent to add `chat: chat as any` (fashion, simple, story, weather, addFile, rateLimiting, agentAsTool), which turns off type checking of the model passed to `Agent`. Fix: keep `LanguageModelV2` and remove the casts.

findings.title: The mock is renamed to V2, but its responses are still in the V1 shape.
findings.body: `MockLanguageModelV2` is now used, but `doGenerate`/`doStream` still return V1-shaped data: `text`, `usage: {completionTokens, promptTokens}`, `logprobs`, `defaultObjectGenerationMode`, and stream parts with `textDelta`. V2 expects `content`, `usage: {inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens}`, and `text-start`/`text-delta` parts with `delta`. The `as LanguageModelV2StreamPart[]` cast hides the mismatch, so tests that depend on generated text or usage are not exercising real v5 behaviour. Also, `LanguageModelV2` types may not be exported from "ai". Fix: rewrite the mock outputs in the V2 format.

findings.title: Tool result `output` is set to a raw string and cast to `any`.
findings.body: In AI SDK v5, a tool-result part's `output` must be a typed object such as `{ type: "text", value }` or `{ type: "json", value }`. Passing the plain `args.response` string through `as any` hides that mismatch, so the stored message may fail validation or be turned into a model prompt incorrectly when the thread continues. Fix: `output: { type: "text", value: args.response }`.

findings.title: Renaming the public action argument breaks existing callers.
findings.body: `uploadFile`'s argument changes from `mimeType` to `mediaType`. Any frontend or client that still sends `mimeType` will now fail Convex argument validation (extra field, missing `mediaType`). The same applies to `askAboutImage` in autoSave.ts. I could not see whether the callers were updated in this PR. If they were not, update them, or keep the public argument name and map it internally.

findings.title: Peer dependency range now accepts any future major version of `ai`.
findings.body: Changing `^5.0.0-beta.29` to `>=5.0.0-beta.29` lets consumers install `ai` v6 or later without a peer warning, even though the library is only built against v5 and future majors will bring breaking API changes. The request does not ask for this. Revert it to a caret range (e.g. `^5.0.0-beta.29 || ^5.0.0`).

held.title: Usage may be recorded as zero if the handler already receives promptTokens/completionTokens.
held.body: This reads `args.usage.inputTokens`/`outputTokens` and falls back to 0. According to the PR, the internal `Usage` schema still uses `promptTokens`/`completionTokens`. If the `UsageHandler` args are typed or populated with that internal shape, `inputTokens` is undefined and every billing row stores 0 prompt and completion tokens without any error. I could not see the `UsageHandler` type. Check which field names the core passes, and avoid `|| 0` defaults that hide a missing field.
